subject: Post-call: BlueOrca embeddings + integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@blueorca.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@blueorca.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: BlueOrca embeddings + integration recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Carlos —

Great to meet earlier today. Short recap + proposed next steps from Redwood so we can align on architecture and timelines.

Key points from the call (summary):
- Use case: semantic search + reranking for product docs + entity-aware suggestions.
- Current provider: VectorCloud (already 1.5M vectors, 1536-dim).
- Goals: parity on relevance, 2x cost reduction target, <100ms p50 search latency for queries.
- Must-haves: secure keying (KMS), VPC/private deployment option for PII data, audit logs.

Redwood recommended approach (high level):
1) Pilot: 100k representative vectors in hosted Redwood for A/B relevance tests.
2) Migration: run side-by-side re-embedding pipeline (VectorCloud -> Redwood embeddings) and compare recall/rerank.
3) Production: either cutover to Redwood embeddings or keep embeddings provider + use Redwood reranker if cost-sensitive.

Technical topics we discussed to validate:
- Vector dimensionality: you mentioned 1536 currently. Redwood supports 1024/1536 profiles; we'll match 1536 if you want identical model dims.
- Normalization: L2 normalization with cosine search recommended; we can normalize at write-time or enable server-side normalization.
- Batching & throughput: recommend 2k-5k vector batch ingestion for initial migration; SDK supports streaming upserts.
- Auth & routing: API key for hosted; for Dedicated/Private we'll provide cert-based auth + VPC peering and policy routing.
- Reranker: we propose a two-stage retrieval (approximate ANN -> Redwood reranker with structured scoring).

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
- Emma: share a representative dataset sample (up to 100k vectors) + a short list of 20 queries and expected top-3 results for evaluation.
- Carlos: confirm compliance box (SOC2 + required network controls) and whether you need Private deployment.
- Ben/Redwood Eng: stand up a sandbox project and provide credentials + an ingestion script.

I attached a compact spec (redwood-embed-lite-specs.pdf) and a migration checklist we can walk through.

Would Tuesday 10am PT for a short setup call work to hand off to our eng team?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
---

From: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@blueorca.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@blueorca.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueOrca embeddings + integration recap & next steps

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful and aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from the infra/ML side before we kick off: 

1) Vector dims: we are indeed on 1536 today (VectorCloud). Would prefer to keep same dimensionality to avoid re-training the downstream models. If Redwood provides a 1536 profile that maps closely to our existing embed model, that would be ideal.

2) Similarity & normalization: we currently L2-normalize on write and use cosine. If Redwood can accept already-normalized vectors that's fine; otherwise we prefer the normalization to happen at ingestion so we keep client code simpler.

3) Batching: our ingestion pipeline emits 1k vectors per batch right now; we can bump to 2k if that helps throughput. Also want to confirm idempotency semantics for upserts (we rely on upsert by external id).

4) Metadata & schema: we keep a small JSON metadata blob per vector (product_id, version, created_at). Will Redwood accept arbitrary metadata fields?

5) Migration strategy: 2 options on our side — a) re-embed all historical content (preferred for quality) or b) use cross-provider mapping and run reranker on top (faster, cheaper). We want Redwood's recommendation and any tooling to help measure recall delta.

We'll attach a 10k sample and some query/expected-result pairs later today. Also loop in procurement once we have a basic pilot scope so they can prep a PO.

—Emma
Emma Hayes
Sr. ML Engineer, BlueOrca Analytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@blueorca.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@blueorca.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueOrca embeddings + integration recap & next steps

Thanks Emma — great questions. Looping in Ava (our embeddings PM) and Ben (account lead) for concrete answers and a short technical note.

Jordan (short note): we will:
- Match 1536-dim embedding profile for parity.
- Support server-side L2 normalization and accept already-normalized vectors (both supported).
- Support idempotent upserts keyed by external_id; upsert will replace vector + metadata by id.
- Allow arbitrary metadata blobs (JSON string). Search/rerank can filter on metadata fields.

Ava / Ben — can you confirm ingestion throughput guidance and a short evaluation plan?

Jordan
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@blueorca.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@blueorca.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueOrca embeddings + integration recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Carlos / Jordan —

Thanks for the details — below are concrete technical recommendations and the evaluation plan we propose.

Embeddings profile:
- Vector dimension: 1536 (we'll map to our 1536-compat profile).
- Normalization: prefer server-side L2 normalization at ingestion for consistency unless you want to pre-normalize; both work identically for cosine.

Ingestion & batching:
- Recommended batch size for bulk migration: 2k vectors per request for best GPU throughput. Our SDK supports an async streaming client; sample script attached in the Drive link.
- Idempotency: upsert by external_id (string). Upsert semantics: replace vector + metadata. If you need merge semantics we can add a merge flag in the pilot.

Search & reranking flow:
- Two-stage retrieval: ANN index (HNSW/IVF) -> Redwood reranker model with structured scoring. Use embeddings cosine + metadata filters.
- If you want to preserve downstream models, run side-by-side A/B with 100k sample. We'll compute: MRR@10, recall@100, and rerank delta.

Migration recommendations:
- Option A (recommended for top quality): full re-embed of historical corpus into Redwood 1536 profile, run A/B evaluation on sample queries.
- Option B (faster, lower cost): keep existing vectors in VectorCloud, route retrieval to current provider and use Redwood reranker on top. This reduces migration effort but may not reach parity depending on embed model differences.

Pilot evaluation plan (we can run this end-to-end):
1) You share 100k sample + 20 labeled queries (you said you'd send 10k first; 100k ideal).
2) Redwood ingests sample (2k batches) into a sandbox project.
3) We run retrieval + rerank tests and produce a short evaluation report with metrics and example mismatches.
4) Joint review to decide re-embed vs hybrid approach.

Security/deployment notes:
- Hosted API: API key + optional workspace-level KMS.
- Private/Dedicated: customer-managed VPC with mTLS for traffic; SAML + SCIM provisioning for users.
- Audit logs and token-level usage available via Console.

I'll attach a short ingestion script and a sample evaluation notebook to the Drive link. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute engineering walkthrough after you drop the sample.

Action items assigned:
- Emma: upload 10k sample today, aim for 100k by EOW (we'll start with 10k to validate).
- Carlos: confirm whether Private deployment is required for pilot (yes/no).
- Ben: I'll send sandbox creds and a short intake form.

I'll keep this thread as the technical record.

Best,
Ava Chen
Product Manager, Embeddings
Redwood Inference
